page.layout: One page of text, one column. Running head with page number 547 at the top right. Set-off Hebrew quotation in the middle of the second paragraph, in four lines. No marginal notes. Catchword "rant" at the lower right.

main_text.p: corrumpi, puncta invenerunt, quibus pronuntiatio efformaretur, & quasi pingeretur. Arabum exemplo existimo commotos, qui cum religione sua varias gentes infecissent Alcoranum punctaverunt, ut barbaros religionis suae amantes, sed linguae ignaros in lectione juvarent. Hoc autem & antiquorum autoritate, & evidentibus rationibus demonstrare possum.

Tiberienses fuisse istos Masorethas, asserunt antiqvi Grammatici; hujus rei optimus testis Aben Esdra, qvi librum compositurus [illegible, ~2 letters] tot evolvit, qvi eum praecesserunt, Grammaticos. Ita in libro צחות [?] capite de Patach minore sive Segol rationem redditurus punctationis insolentis כן מיהג חכמי טב דיא ותם העקר כיטהם היו אנשי המסרה ואגהנו מהם [illegible, ~2 letters] קבלו המגקד ויכתסק לורנהם העקר כי טהם אולי עאי קשלא י חשוב ארם בי שכח [?] clarius id docere non potuit Aben Esdra; à Tiberiensibus igitur omnis punctatio. Tiberienses autem illi numero e-

page.notes: The Hebrew quotation sits inside the paragraph and runs in four printed lines; it is copied here inline and its letter forms are doubtful throughout, so every uncertain word is marked [?]. Two boxed glyphs in the Hebrew (after "compositurus" and in the second line after "מהם") look like missing or damaged type and are given as illegible. The catchword "rant" completes the hyphenated "e-" at the line end. The last full printed line ends with "e-", so the paragraph stops there. Spelling such as "qvi", "antiqvi" and "qvibus" is kept as printed.
